description.summary: A Japanese yokai that manifests as an invisible wall blocking travelers' paths at night. The nurikabe prevents passage in any direction until defeated by tapping its lower portion with a stick.
description.full: The nurikabe is a peculiar yokai from Japanese folklore that appears as an invisible barrier in the paths of nighttime travelers. When a person encounters a nurikabe, they find themselves unable to proceed forward, backward, or to either side—an invisible wall blocks every direction they attempt. The frustrated traveler may wander in circles or attempt various routes, all to no avail. According to tradition, the only way to bypass a nurikabe is to tap the lower part of the invisible barrier with a stick, at which point it vanishes. While usually depicted as invisible, some artistic representations show the nurikabe as a large, wall-like creature with eyes and sometimes limbs. The nurikabe serves as a yokai explanation for becoming inexplicably lost or blocked while traveling at night, particularly on dark roads. In modern times, the nurikabe appears in yokai collections, video games (notably inspiring aspects of Pokémon characters), and Japanese popular culture. The nurikabe represents the supernatural obstacles and confusions that travelers might encounter, teaching patience and problem-solving while adding mystery to nighttime journeys.
